newsitem.title: FRANCE: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 18.
newsitem.headline: Reuters French Advertising & Media Digest - Aug 18.

text.p: News from Reuters and the French press on Advertising, Media & the Internet and Brand-name Products.

PARIS - Shares in French media group Pathe fall sharply on Monday after a slide on Friday in shares of television company British Sky Broadcasting Group Plc. Pathe has 17 percent stake in BSkyB which issued a profit warning on Friday with its first half results. (Reuter)

MADRID - Spanish pay television group Sogecable reaches a deal with Universal Studios over film and "pay per view" rights and a new action-suspense channel. The deal will allow it to broadcast Universal films on pay-TV channel Canal Plus. (Reuter)

PARIS - The Amaury press group plans to launch a TV sports news channel using the expertise of its daily sports newspaper L'Equipe and Amaury Sports Organisation, its unit which organises sporting events. (Les Echos)

PARIS - CanalSatellite is offering new subscribers a free satellite dish from August 20 to October 31, a new initiative in the war for subscribers between France's two leading digital satellite services. (Les Echos)

LONDON - FCA! advertising agency says its recent merger with a UK-based branding specialist will help it grow across Europe and satisfy growing client demand for "through-the-line" service. Impact FCA! in London was renamed FCA! after its French parent company, Publicis SA, bought Kelly Weedon Shute agency in July. (Reuter)

NEW YORK - CUC International Inc., seeking to extend its reach in global online commerce, agrees to acquire Paris-based classified advertising publisher Hebdo Mag International in a stock swap worth $440 million.(Reuter)

LONDON - A new dimension of virtual imagery is set to revolutionise television advertising at major world sports and cultural events. Allied Domecq used the new technology in Britain in July to display virtual images of brand logos on boards at each end of the pitch in a satellite TV broadcast of the England versus Australia rugby game. The EPSIS virtual advertising system was developed by Syma Vision, a unit of Lagardere Groupe in France.(Reuter)

SOFIA - Danone-Serdika, the Bulgarian subsidiary of France's Danone Group, says it is to continue its activity in Bulgaria despite huge losses caused by the problems of the local dairy farming sector. (Reuter)
PARIS - France could top last year's record for the number of foreign tourists visiting the country in 1997. (Le Parisien)
